 ’80s singer’s tour cancelled after ‘disgusting’ comments defending Russell Brand 
 Lauren Attard Updated November 12, 2026 - 8.13am . First published at 3.06am 
 shares Share article Ian McNabb, lead singer of 1980s rock band Icicle Works, has had several upcoming shows cancelled after sharing a now-deleted post defending convicted rapist Russell Brand. 
 Brand, 51, has dominated headlines after he was jailed for 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assaults on November 9. Following McNabb’s public support of the disgraced comedian, many of his British show dates were dropped. 
 80’s rocker Ian McNabb, lead singer of Icicle Works, has had several dates of his upcoming tour scrapped after sharing comments in defence of convicted rapist Russell Brand.   Facebook/Ian McNabb 
 Advertisement In posts across his Facebook and X accounts , McNabb, 66, claimed Brand was “stitched up” for his “outspoken views”. McNabb’s posts have since been removed. 
 “He got close to the target,” McNabb wrote at the time. “And he has a big audience. I know people who were in his orbit and girls were throwing themselves at him every night.” 
 McNabb continued: “If that happened to me I know what I’d do. If you want to hang out with the artist don’t cry when you’re in the picture. All the chicks who turn up at these situations know exactly what’s going on.”
 “The ones who decided they were done badly to – ten years after the event – are the worst.” 
 Read more
 Jonathan Ross breaks silence on David Walliams allegations, Russell Brand crimes 
 McNabb’s defence of Brand angered several venue owners who had scheduled his upcoming tour dates. His appearances at The Cluny 2 in Newcastle, Cottiers in Glasgow and The Voodoo Rooms in Edinburgh have since been scrapped, with refunds available. 
 Concert promoter Ewan McNaught, who booked several of McNabb’s shows, has also cut ties with him following his “disgusting comments” supporting Brand. 
 “I hate cancelling gigs, and it’s one of the few times in my career that I’ve had to do it, but not only can I not defend Ian McNabb’s disgraceful social media comments in support of Russell Brand, as a husband and a father of a young daughter, I simply can’t work with him moving forward,” McNaught wrote. 
 Advertisement McNaught detailed he spoke with McNabb’s agent and venues who are “all on the same page” on the matter. 
 McNabb’s concert promoter Ewan McNaught issued this statement condemning his support of Brand.   Facebook/Ewan McNaught 
 McNabb issued another statement which has also been deleted claiming he and his shows had been “cancelled”.   Facebook/Ian McNabb 
 McNaught warned that he expected more of McNabb’s upcoming shows to be cancelled. 
 Advertisement Advertisement He added: “I’d like to emphasise that it wasn’t a unilateral decision. There was a broad consensus between agent, promoter and venues that these shows simply couldn’t go ahead under the circumstances.” 
 The comments under McNaught’s statement applauded the team for making “100 per cent the right call”. 
 “I imagine this was a hard call, even given what’s been said. But I think it’s absolutely the right thing to do and I absolutely support your decision,” one wrote. 
 Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months jail for rape and sexual assault against six women.  AP Photo/Kin Cheung 
 Advertisement Another commented: “It’s a relief to see more men outwardly reject this crap. It’s hard enough for women to get a break in this industry but many of us are survivors.” 
 McNabb disclosed that both he and his upcoming shows were “cancelled”, in an attempt to offer an explanation and apology. That statement has also since been removed from his social media accounts. 
 nine.com.au has contacted McNabb’s representative for further comment. 
 Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic and Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) .
